subject: english
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The principal was ADAMANT that no student would leave before the closing bell.
explanation: Adamant means refusing to change your mind, so "unyielding" is the closest in meaning.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: Ada is METICULOUS in keeping her lecture notes.
explanation: Meticulous means paying very careful attention to detail, which is what "painstaking" means.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The instruction on the registration form was AMBIGUOUS.
explanation: Something ambiguous can be understood in more than one way, so "unclear" is the nearest meaning.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: Typewriters have become OBSOLETE in most offices.
explanation: Obsolete describes something no longer in use because something newer has replaced it, so "outdated" is correct.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The fans were JUBILANT after the Super Eagles' victory.
explanation: Jubilant means feeling or expressing great happiness, so "overjoyed" is the closest.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: I appreciate your CANDID assessment of my essay.
explanation: A candid assessment is open and honest, so "frank" is the nearest in meaning.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: The afternoon heat made everyone in the hall feel LETHARGIC.
explanation: Lethargic means lacking energy, so "sluggish" is the closest meaning.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: Only a TENACIOUS candidate can master all these topics in one month.
explanation: Tenacious means not giving up easily, which is what "persistent" means.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: My grandmother has lived a FRUGAL life since she retired.
explanation: Frugal means careful not to waste money, so "thrifty" is correct. "Wasteful" is its opposite.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option nearest in meaning to the word in capitals: With the heavy rain, flooding on that road was INEVITABLE.
explanation: Inevitable means certain to happen, so "unavoidable" is the nearest meaning. "Avoidable" is the opposite.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: Chief Okafor is known to be GENEROUS to the poor.
explanation: Generous means willing to give freely. Its opposite is "stingy", meaning unwilling to give.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: Observers said the election process was TRANSPARENT.
explanation: A transparent process is open for everyone to see, so the opposite is "secretive".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: Yams were ABUNDANT during the harvest season.
explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantities. The opposite is "scarce". "Plentiful" means the same as abundant.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: Despite his success, the musician remained HUMBLE.
explanation: Humble means not thinking you are better than others. The opposite is "arrogant".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: Use of English is COMPULSORY for all UTME candidates.
explanation: Compulsory means something you must do. The opposite is "optional", meaning you may choose.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The closure of the bridge is only TEMPORARY.
explanation: Temporary means lasting for a limited time. The opposite is "permanent".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: Funke is a DILIGENT student.
explanation: Diligent means hardworking and careful. The opposite is "lazy".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The hotel lobby was decorated with ARTIFICIAL flowers.
explanation: Artificial means made by people rather than occurring in nature. The opposite is "natural".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: Emeka was RELUCTANT to lend out his textbook.
explanation: Reluctant means unwilling. The opposite is "eager", meaning keen to do something.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option opposite in meaning to the word in capitals: The coach was OPTIMISTIC about the final match.
explanation: Optimistic means expecting a good outcome. The opposite is "pessimistic", expecting a bad one.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: If I ___ you, I would accept the scholarship.
explanation: An imaginary condition ("If I were you") takes "were" for every subject in formal English.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: By the time we arrived at the hall, the lecture ___.
explanation: The lecture began before another past action (our arrival), so the past perfect "had started" is needed.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: She has been living in Abuja ___ 2019.
explanation: Use "since" with a point in time (2019) and "for" with a length of time (seven years).

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The students were warned to desist ___ noise-making.
explanation: The verb "desist" is always followed by "from": to desist from doing something.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The man ___ car was stolen reported the matter to the police.
explanation: The car belongs to the man, and "whose" is the relative pronoun that shows possession.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: I look forward to ___ from you soon.
explanation: In "look forward to", "to" is a preposition, so it is followed by the -ing form: "hearing".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Tobi is the ___ of the two brothers.
explanation: When comparing exactly two people, use the comparative form "taller", not the superlative.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: We have run ___ of fuel, so we must stop at the next filling station.
explanation: To "run out" of something means to have none left, so "out" is correct.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Hardly had the bell rung ___ the students rushed out of the class.
explanation: "Hardly" is paired with "when" in this structure: Hardly had X happened when Y happened. ("No sooner" is paired with "than".)

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The doctor advised him to abstain ___ alcohol.
explanation: The verb "abstain" takes the preposition "from": to abstain from something.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Neither of the boys ___ been to Lagos before.
explanation: "Neither of" refers to one person at a time, so it takes a singular verb: "has".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Each of the candidates ___ given a pencil and an answer sheet.
explanation: "Each" refers to one candidate at a time, so the singular verb "was" is correct.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The news from the village ___ very encouraging.
explanation: "News" looks plural but is an uncountable noun, so it takes the singular verb "is".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
explanation: "Mathematics" is the name of one subject, so it takes the singular verb "is".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Bread and butter ___ his usual breakfast.
explanation: "Bread and butter" is thought of as one meal, so it takes the singular verb "is".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: One of the girls ___ lost her bag.
explanation: The subject is "one", not "girls", so the singular verb "has" is correct.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: Either the teacher or the students ___ to blame for the noise.
explanation: With "either ... or", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. "Students" is plural, so use "are".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best completes the sentence: The number of applicants ___ increased this year.
explanation: "The number of" is singular, so it takes "has". ("A number of applicants" would be plural.)

subject: english
stem: Choose the correct question tag: He hardly ever comes late, ___?
explanation: "Hardly" makes the sentence negative, so the tag must be positive: "does he".

subject: english
stem: Choose the correct question tag: Let's go to the library, ___?
explanation: A suggestion that starts with "Let's" always takes the tag "shall we".

subject: english
stem: Choose the correct question tag: You are coming with us, ___?
explanation: A positive statement with "are" takes a negative tag with the same verb: "aren't you".

subject: english
stem: Choose the correct question tag: She can swim very well, ___?
explanation: The statement is positive and uses "can", so the tag is negative with the same helping verb: "can't she".

subject: english
stem: Choose the correct question tag: Nobody called while I was out, ___?
explanation: "Nobody" makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive, and "nobody" is replaced by "they": "did they".

subject: english
stem: Choose the correct question tag: I am your friend, ___?
explanation: The accepted negative tag for "I am" is "aren't I".

subject: english
stem: Choose the correct question tag: They have finished the project, ___?
explanation: A positive statement with "have" takes a negative tag with the same verb: "haven't they".

subject: english
stem: Choose the correct question tag: The boys never listen to advice, ___?
explanation: "Never" makes the statement negative, so the tag is positive: "do they".

subject: english

options: a costly project that is of little use
explanation: A white elephant is something that costs a lot to build or maintain but is of little use: "a costly project that is of little use".

subject: english

options: caught in the act of stealing
caught with blood on his hands
explanation: To be caught red-handed means to be "caught in the act of stealing" or doing something wrong.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes: Tunde "let the cat out of the bag" about the surprise party.
explanation: To let the cat out of the bag means to give away a secret, so Tunde "revealed the secret".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes: For Amaka, the mathematics test was "a piece of cake".
explanation: Something that is a piece of cake is "very easy" to do.

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes: After his suspension, Chidi decided to "turn over a new leaf".
options: change his behaviour for the better
explanation: To turn over a new leaf means to make a fresh start, that is, to "change his behaviour for the better".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes: Stop "beating about the bush" and tell me what happened.
explanation: To beat about the bush means to talk around a subject while "avoiding the main point".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes: Voters took the politician's promises "with a pinch of salt".
explanation: To take something with a pinch of salt means to doubt how true it is, so the voters "accepted them with doubt".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes: At the end of the dinner, my uncle "footed the bill".
explanation: To foot the bill means to pay for something, so he "paid the bill".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes: Bisi "burnt the midnight oil" before her UTME.
explanation: To burn the midnight oil means to work or study late at night, so she "studied late into the night".

subject: english
stem: Choose the option that best explains the expression in quotes: The plan to build a new hostel "fell through".
explanation: When a plan falls through, it fails to happen, so the plan "failed".
